note: Exactly TWO bridge experiments per the pilot rule: BR-A sensing-weighted, BR-B power-weighted. Both are unifications-and-deepenings of the existing ladders with traceable lineage IDs (B15 BT-x, B25 PB-x, B10-cited corpus falsification tests FT-x); neither is invented fresh. Ranking criteria per the stage spec: information gain, reusability, time, cost, safety, publication value, commercial evidence, dependency. All cost/time figures are EST order-of-magnitude planning labels carried from the cited B25/B15/B10 records, not quotes or measurements. Safety paragraphs are research planning, not safety approvals (SOURCE_POLICY). Idea IDs are verbatim from the A30/B20 universe; W1/W2 are B25 POWER.md §9 wedges; S1-S5 are this pilot's SKILLS.csv rows.
ranking_rationale_summary: BR-A ranks 1 because its Phase 0 is zero-cost, zero-dependency, and epistemically upstream: the corpus's own rule (C31/C48) is that FT-02 gates every dollar after it, and the estimator-honesty discipline it validates is load-bearing for BOTH bridges' frozen-analysis controls and for the entire W2 detection lane. BR-B ranks 2 despite the higher commercial-evidence value (it unifies B25's own ladder ranks 1 and 2) because it costs $11-35K EST combined, depends on the missing skill S3 being trained to supervised competence and on reference-chain access, and carries the ladder's highest safety burden. This ordering follows the shared B15 §5 / B25 criterion: cheapest decisive gate first.

bridges.rank_rationale: Highest decision leverage per dollar on the unified ladder: Phase 0 costs $0, has no dependencies, and per the corpus's own rule (C31/C48: FT-02 'gates every dollar after it') must pass before any estimator-based claim — PhD Element 3, W2 detection statistics, or either bridge's frozen-analysis discipline — is credible. Phase 1 then buys the corpus-documented first bench test of the reverse direction (EV32/M2) for $1-5K EST. B15 ranked its two components 1st (BT-1) and 3rd (BT-3) of eight; unifying them preserves that ordering logic while making the desk gate an explicit stop/continue gate for the bench spend.
bridges.name: Estimator-honesty-gated reverse-direction ladder: desk FT-02 honesty test, then bench coil-referenced Hall-gain recovery
bridges.hypothesis: (a) An estimator built to the T0 specification (C10) can be made provably honest: on Theorem-1 non-identifiable scenarios (C23) it freezes the affected states and inflates its reported covariance instead of silently converging on its prior (the FM-18 failure mode, C24); and (b) given a trusted coil/current excursion chain, Hall GAIN is recoverable within the Fisher-predicted interval while offset recovery is structurally refused — the reverse (coil-informs-Hall) direction that the B15 corpus shows has never been tested even at bench level (EV32/M2; C26 gap b; single non-fusion precedent per C30).
protocol: Phase 0, step 1 (desk): build a minimal T0 estimator skeleton per the C10 module boundary (model/schema/estimator/scenarios/metrics only; no scope growth).

Phase 0, step 2: implement the Theorem-1 non-identifiable scenarios (C23 CASE-A class: unreferenced Hall+coil pair, constant gains/offsets) and at least one identifiable control case (known machine-current field model at >=2 field levels, per C23's full-rank case).
Phase 0, step 3: pre-register pass criteria and freeze the analysis configuration before any run (FT-02 discipline).

Phase 0, step 4: run and record — the estimator must freeze the non-identifiable states and inflate reported covariance on the Theorem-1 scenarios while converging normally on the identifiable control case.

Phase 0, step 5: wrong-prior cross-check — rerun the non-identifiable scenarios with deliberately wrong priors and verify the estimator visibly flags non-identifiability rather than confidently tracking whichever prior it was handed.
GATE (stop/continue): Phase 1 starts only on a Phase 0 pass (see stop_continue_gate).

Phase 1, step 6 (bench): establish a trusted excursion chain — programmed current ramps through a calibrated field coil driving a known field excursion at a co-mounted Hall/coil sensor pair; reference the coil chain against the best available certificated DC chain (BR-B's reference chain if available; a calibrated coil chain alone at reduced, disclosed grade otherwise).
Phase 1, step 7: vary excursion profiles (rate, amplitude, dwell) per the C23 identifiability case structure to test its predictions, not just a single operating point.
Phase 1, step 8: recover Hall gain via the FT-05 protocol with the frozen, pre-registered analysis; compare the recovered gain against the Fisher-predicted interval (C23).
Phase 1, step 9: swap the reference between certificated and uncertificated chains and verify that recovery quality tracks reference trust as predicted (the point of the C23/EV32 discipline).
Phase 1, step 10: verify the estimator REFUSES offset recovery throughout (Theorem-1 discipline — offset is never claimed recoverable from the pair alone).

Device honesty note: Phase 1's gain-recovery target is a commercial Hall sensor by default; the PhD's GaN die is optional and included ONLY if the C04 anomaly has closed — the experiment is decision-grade without it (same non-gating design as B25 PB-1).
metrics: Phase 0: state-freeze and covariance-inflation behavior on each non-identifiable scenario (binary per scenario, plus reported-covariance ratio vs the near-truth-initialized run); convergence error on the identifiable control case; wrong-prior divergence visibility flag.

Phase 1: recovered-gain error vs the Fisher-predicted interval (inside/outside, and margin); degradation ratio of recovery quality between certificated and uncertificated reference chains vs prediction; offset-refusal check (binary); excursion-profile dependence of recovery quality vs C23 case predictions.
controls: Identifiable control scenarios run alongside every non-identifiable scenario (the estimator must not be trivially inert).
Wrong-prior reruns (Phase 0 step 5) to expose silent prior-tracking — the specific failure mode FM-18 names as invisible in near-truth-initialized simulations (C24).
Analysis configuration and pass criteria frozen and pre-registered before data/runs in both phases.
Reference-chain swap (certificated vs uncertificated) as a positive control that the method detects reference quality.
Excursion-profile variation as a structural control against single-point luck.
Mutual Hall/coil consistency used as consistency ONLY; every absolute statement routes through the referenced chain (C23/C07 discipline; EV32).
bridges.success_gate: Phase 0: the estimator passes FT-02 verbatim — frozen states plus inflated covariance on all Theorem-1 scenarios, normal convergence on identifiable controls, and wrong-prior runs visibly flagged. Phase 1: recovered gain lands inside the Fisher-predicted interval with the trusted chain, degrades as predicted with the untrusted chain, and offset recovery is refused throughout — a clean first bench test of the reverse direction (corpus-bounded claim; FT-01 kill search still required before any publication novelty claim, per B15's honesty rule).
bridges.kill_gate: Phase 0 kill: if after one documented redesign attempt the estimator still converges confidently on non-identifiable scenarios, ALL estimator-based claims stop — Opt2 Element 3's integrity premise, the W2 detection-statistics lane, and both bridges' analysis discipline are unsupported until fixed; per C31 this single desk result gates every dollar after it. Phase 1 kill: if gain recovery fails WITH the trusted chain, the C26 gap (b) reverse-direction claims retire and the architecture collapses to the proven forward direction — itself a clean, publishable negative result (B15 BT-3's own framing).
bridges.dependencies: Phase 0: none — desk-only, $0, independent of C04, C45, HSX machine time, and all purchases. Phase 1: field coil + programmable current source (bench tier); benefits from BR-B's certificated reference chain but can run without it at reduced, disclosed grade; GaN-die inclusion (optional, non-gating) requires C04 closure; partner-tier variant (magnet-lab drive) is a collaboration ask, not a purchase.
bridges.time: Phase 0: desk-days-to-weeks EST. Phase 1: 2-4 bench-weeks EST (B25 PB-5).
bridges.cost_range: $0 (Phase 0) + $1-5K EST incremental at bench tier (Phase 1, B25 PB-5: field coil, fixtures); partner tier adds no purchase cost.
bridges.safety: Phase 0: none (desk). Phase 1: low-voltage bench practice; if hosted on BR-B's converter-driven bed, BR-B's full safety regime applies (interlocks, capacitor-discharge verification, staged escalation, supervision per S3); partner tier inherits the host lab's stored-energy safety regime — the founder does not run magnet hardware. Research planning, not a safety approval.
bridges.phd_value: Executes B15's #1-ranked (BT-1) and #3-ranked (BT-3) tests in one ladder; FT-02 is the corpus's own highest-priority, lowest-cost gate for the whole Opt2 program (C31/C48); Phase 1 is, per the corpus, the first bench test of the reverse direction (EV32/M2 — corpus-bounded) and directly tests C23's predictions; converts S5 from literature_backed_near_transfer to current_demonstrated; fully independent of HSX scheduling; either Phase 1 outcome is publishable (positive first-test or clean negative).
bridges.startup_value: De-risks the W2 detection/estimator lane: P3R2-D-01 and ST01-C11's shared false-trigger methodology is exactly this honesty discipline; F-02's reverse sliver and F-06's magnet leg (trusted excursion capture) get their method evidence; ST01-C10's test-stand lane gains a demonstrated qualification competence; keeps the OPT3 fallback (C47) and the CN-01-class far-domain reconstruction market live as options. A Phase 0 kill is equally decisive commercially: it retires every W2 estimator claim before any customer conversation.
bridges.dual_use_rationale: One methodology — identifiability-aware estimation with pre-registered honesty tests — is simultaneously Opt2 Element 3's integrity gate (PhD) and the qualification-statistics core of W2 detection products (startup). It is option-preserving: it serves the current thesis, the OPT3 fallback direction, multiple startup rows (D-01, ST01-C11, F-02, F-06), and transfers to far domains per the CN-01 record, while committing zero dollars until its own desk gate passes.
bridges.stop_continue_gate: G-BR-A-0 (after Phase 0): PASS → proceed to Phase 1 and unblock estimator-based claims elsewhere; FAIL → one documented redesign attempt allowed; second FAIL → durable stop on all estimator claims and descope to the anchor-only architecture (the corpus's own good-outcome descope pattern, C25). G-BR-A-1 (after Phase 1): PASS → carry the credential to W2 and to the publication route (subject to disclosure gates C34 and FT-01 kill search); FAIL with trusted chain → stop all reverse-direction claims, keep the forward direction, write up the negative result.

bridges.rank_rationale: The highest commercial-evidence item on the unified ladder — it merges B25's own ranks 1 and 2 (PB-1, PB-2) and B15's BT-6, producing the decisive datum for the competing-channel question (C43/M6/G5-gap) AND the W1 wedge's producibility test in one campaign. It ranks 2 rather than 1 because it costs $11-35K EST combined, requires the missing skill S3 to reach supervised competence first, needs reference-chain access (borrow/rent/buy), and carries the ladder's highest safety burden — every one of which BR-A Phase 0 avoids. Reusability is the counterweight: its bed, reference chain, and GUM template are reused by BR-A Phase 1 and every full-run PB-3/PB-4 successor.
bridges.name: Traceable DC current-channel benchmark under WBG switching EMI, closed with an uncertainty-budgeted acceptance dossier
bridges.hypothesis: (a) A traceable reference chain (certificated zero-flux/fluxgate transducer + wideband coaxial shunt) whose combined uncertainty demonstrably closes below the inter-technology differences can decide whether Hall-class DC-capable channels meet, miss, or tie the TMR class against P0050-derived requirement classes inside an operating WBG switching cell — the head-to-head the corpus shows nobody has published (M6/G5; decisive for C43); and (b) the founder can personally produce a signed, uncertainty-budgeted acceptance dossier on purchased instruments at a quality a third party could re-execute — the W1 wedge's commercial premise (EV01 shows the skill is scarce; EV35/G3/M3).
protocol: Step 1 (pre-flight): commission one WBG half-bridge evaluation cell (SiC or GaN) at 48-100 V bus under supervision (S3 path); interlock checklist, capacitor-discharge verification, staged escalation only with qualified supervision; 400 V-class explicitly deferred.

Step 2: assemble the reference chain — zero-flux/fluxgate transducer of merchant calibration grade with calibration certificate (borrowed/rented preferred; the S-B25-02 vendor class exists) plus wideband coaxial shunt for edge fidelity (P0048/P0056 class); construct the reference chain's OWN GUM budget per the EV01/P0008 template — a direct small-scale exercise of WP-C methodology (C06) on a current measurand, not gated by C04.
Step 3: pre-register pass/fail thresholds against P0050-derived requirement classes and freeze all analysis scripts BEFORE data taking (FT-02-style discipline imported from BR-A Phase 0).
Step 4: static DC sweeps over rated range vs the zero-flux reference — gain/offset with uncertainty budget, for commercial Hall head(s) and commercial TMR head (EV28's incumbent class).
Step 5: small-signal frequency response via injected ripple at fixed DC bias.
Step 6: double-pulse edge capture vs the coaxial shunt (amplitude/settling/delay).

Step 7: EMI susceptibility — error vs switching state at MEASURED (not assumed) dV/dt and dI/dt, fixed distances/orientations; repeated at zero sensed current (pure pickup); position/orientation swaps.
Step 8: temperature drift over a stated chamber-limited range plus an 8-24 h soak at constant conditions; switching-disabled DC-only runs at matched dissipation to separate thermal from EMI effects.

Step 9 (dossier phase, PB-2): full GUM budget of the complete purchased chain with every component named; repeat-measurement campaign (>=3 full re-setups) testing the budget's reproducibility term; deliberately perturbed setup (cable swap, position shift) to test whether the budget catches its own stated sensitivities; second-analyst pass or interval re-derivation on the raw data; written acceptance dossier in the G-03 artifact format (protocol, results, budget, pass/fail against a pre-stated spec class).

Device honesty note: the PhD's GaN die with the C13 readout chain is OPTIONAL and non-gating, included only if C04 has closed; the experiment is decision-grade with commercial sensors alone (B25 PB-1 design carried verbatim).
metrics: Reference-chain combined uncertainty vs the inter-technology differences being resolved (the decision-grade criterion).

Per-channel table: DC transfer accuracy (gain/offset with budget), usable small-signal bandwidth, transient fidelity vs shunt, EMI-induced error vs switching state at measured edge rates, temperature/soak drift.
Dossier phase: repeat-campaign results vs the pre-stated budget at stated coverage; perturbation-detection outcome; dossier completeness/reproducibility assessment (could a third party re-execute).
controls: Reference channels shielded and cross-checked in the overlap band; mutual consistency treated as consistency ONLY — absoluteness enters solely through the certificated chain (C23/Theorem-1 discipline).
Sensor-absent and current-absent runs for noise/pickup floors.
Position/orientation swaps to separate conductor-geometry sensitivity (EV17 class) from technology-intrinsic error.
Switching-disabled DC-only runs at matched dissipation (thermal vs EMI separation).
Pass/fail thresholds pre-registered against P0050's requirement synthesis (EV27) before data taking; analysis scripts frozen first.
Dossier phase: budget frozen BEFORE the repeat campaign; deliberate setup perturbations; independent second pass on raw data.
bridges.success_gate: A defensible, uncertainty-budgeted comparison table in which the combined reference uncertainty is demonstrably smaller than the inter-technology differences resolved, yielding a clear verdict on Hall-class vs TMR-class channels against P0050-derived requirement classes under switching EMI (closing M6/G5 for this evidence base); AND the repeat campaign lands inside the pre-stated budget at the stated coverage with a dossier complete enough for third-party re-execution (the W1 producibility premise held).
bridges.kill_gate: Methodological kill: the reference chain's achieved uncertainty cannot close below the Hall-vs-TMR differences — the benchmark is not decision-grade; stop, report, fix the chain before any claim. Wedge kill: BOTH channel classes' EMI-induced error under realistic switching exceeds their claimed accuracy class by margins no bolt-on calibration repairs — the calibrated-telemetry slivers of P3R2-C-01/C-13 die as differentiators and F-06's magnetics-adjacent modality option dies with them (B20's stated falsifier); the zero-flux/FOCS incumbent path stands. Dossier kill: repeats fall outside the budget and the discrepancy cannot be attributed within the budget's own terms — the C06-class methodology claim is not credible at even bench scale; no W1 customer conversation until fixed. GaN-die kill (only if included): die performance uncompetitive with commercial Hall confirms any GaN-sensor power story is packaging/environment-based, not performance-based (EV11).
bridges.dependencies: S3 (missing skill) trained to supervised test-bed competence — a hard pre-flight gate; qualified supervision or power-electronics-lab partnership arranged (part of the design, not optional); reference-transducer access with calibration certificate (borrow/rent/buy; dominant cost item); temperature chamber or controlled enclosure for drift runs; BR-A Phase 0's frozen-analysis discipline (soft dependency — imported, and independently required by the corpus's own rule); explicitly NOT gated by C04, C45, or HSX machine time.
bridges.time: 3-6 bench-weeks EST (benchmark, B25 PB-1) + 2-3 bench-weeks EST (dossier phase, B25 PB-2), plus analysis; calendar placement on PREP_PLAN days 91-365.
bridges.cost_range: $8-25K EST (PB-1 breakdown: WBG cell/gate drive ~$1-3K, commercial Hall/TMR heads hundreds, coaxial shunt ~$1-2K, zero-flux reference the dominant item at $5-15K purchase EST or much less borrowed/rented, fixtures ~$1-2K) + $3-10K EST incremental for the dossier phase (PB-2). All EST, carried from B25's records.
bridges.safety: Bench power-electronics practice per B25 PB-1: interlocked/enclosed DUT, capacitor-discharge verification before touching, rated differential/isolated probes, no live probing at elevated bus, staged voltage escalation, thermal monitoring. Honest note carried verbatim: safe practice at elevated DC bus is a competence NOT evidenced in B10's ledger — supervision or partnership with a power-electronics lab is part of the design. The 48-100 V start and deferred 400 V-class are deliberate safety boundaries. Research planning, not a safety approval.
bridges.phd_value: Closes B15 gaps M6/G5 (a head-to-head the corpus's own review layer calls for and nobody has published); informs C43 (TMR as the sharpest single-channel challenger to the PhD's value proposition); exercises WP-C-class uncertainty budgeting (C06) on a bench current measurand independent of C04; produces a worked GUM template directly transferable to the WP-C field-measurand version (S2 acceleration); plausible instrumentation-comparison publication regardless of any venture; converts S1's extension target and part of S2's target into evidence.
bridges.startup_value: W1's product motion rehearsed end-to-end: G-03 (the dossier IS its product), F-06 (modality question answered in both directions — B20's named falsifier), C-05 (method-authority class shown to generalize), D-09 (traceability rehearsal); W2's measurement chain: ST01-C10 and ST03-ID_08/ID_12 (whether magnetics-adjacent channels belong in the precision chain at all); the C-01/C-13 calibrated-telemetry slivers' explicit upgrade-or-die condition; feeds B40 the decisive datum B15's BT-6 anticipated. Kill outcomes are equally decision-grade for B40.
bridges.dual_use_rationale: The same traceable GUM discipline is Opt2 Element 1's credential (PhD) and W1's sellable artifact class (startup); the same benchmark dataset serves an instrumentation publication and wedge collateral; the bed, reference chain, and frozen-analysis templates are reused by BR-A Phase 1 and every full-run PB-3/PB-4 successor. Option-preserving: it advances the PhD's calibration program sideways (not gated by C04), keeps both wedges testable, and its wedge-kill outcome cleanly retires two idea families before any capital is committed to them.
bridges.stop_continue_gate: G-BR-B-pre (pre-flight): supervised-competence sign-off (S3) AND certificated reference access in hand → start; either missing → do NOT start (no unsupervised elevated-bus work; no uncertificated 'benchmark'). G-BR-B-mid (methodological): reference uncertainty fails to close below inter-technology differences → pause, fix the chain, publish nothing. G-BR-B-exit: benchmark + dossier both pass → continue W1 (and carry the modality verdict to B40); dossier fails → stop all W1 customer-facing steps until the methodology is credible at bench scale; wedge kill fires → retire the calibrated-telemetry slivers and the F-06 magnetics-adjacent option, report the negative result to B40 — informative either way.
